newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope tells people to be brave in face of cold.
newsitem.headline: Pope tells people to be brave in face of cold.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Sunday urged people to be brave during freezing cold weather which has swept large parts of Europe and the United States.
"It seems the world is cold, also here in Italy, but more so in the north," the Pope told pilgrims gathered in the courtyard of his residence near Rome to hear the weekly Angelus message.
"I hope you are courageous in the face of the cold. Warm yourselves up," he said.
"It seems that today you can hear the wind more than the Pope," he added, holding on to his white papal cap to prevent it being blown away.
Temperatures have dipped as low as minus 30 Celsius (minus 22 Fahrenheit) in Italy's northern mountains.
Heavy snow fell in the central regions of Tuscany and Umbria overnight, blocking roads and isolating remote villages. Snow flurries were also reported in the usually mild Rome.
Conditions have been more extreme in the north of Europe. The western USA has also been buffeted by winter storms over the past week.
